description: Curated reference library of high-quality design work, tagged by what specifically makes each entry work. Used as RAG context before generation.

entries.name: Stripe Homepage
entries.what_makes_it_work: Absolute typographic restraint — uses only weight and size variation, never color, to establish hierarchy. The primary H1 stays mid-weight, not bold. Grid lines are structural, not decorative.
specific_techniques: color used only for brand moments not layout

entries.name: Linear App
entries.what_makes_it_work: The dark surface is textured, not flat — subtle noise and gradient banding create depth without adding visual clutter. Every screenshot of the product is shown at oblique angles, making static UI feel kinetic.

entries.name: Vercel Homepage
entries.what_makes_it_work: Pure black and white with absolute color discipline — the ONLY chromatic element is the product UI itself shown in the hero. This makes the product the sole visual subject. Typography is set at extreme scales, using contrast of scale as the primary compositional device.

entries.name: Figma Homepage
entries.what_makes_it_work: Uses a deliberately varied set of colors, but applies them structurally — each feature or person gets a distinct color treatment, so variety becomes organization, not chaos.

entries.name: Loom Homepage
entries.what_makes_it_work: A very specific, ownable shade of purple (not Tailwind violet) used consistently and nowhere else. The hero uses real video stills, not illustrations, grounding the product promise in real use.

entries.name: Craft Docs
entries.what_makes_it_work: Applies the App Store aesthetic — large, full-bleed photography with product UI overlaid. Uses the typography convention of display italic for emotional counterpoint to the otherwise rigid sans-serif system.

entries.name: Arc Browser
entries.what_makes_it_work: Uses a strongly saturated, warm gradient (not cool) that is completely off-trend for developer tools — it reads as a genuine personality statement. Copy is in first person and conversational, breaking the SaaS convention.

entries.name: Pitch
entries.what_makes_it_work: The dark background is a genuine design choice — it mirrors the dark mode users will actually work in, making the product promise (beautiful presentations) feel immediately credible. Uses very large, ultra-light type at section transitions.

entries.name: Revolut Homepage
entries.what_makes_it_work: Uses motion as a core information carrier — the card animation in the hero is not decorative, it shows the product's core value (any currency, any card) in 3 seconds without text. Layout uses actual financial data as background texture.

entries.name: Framer
entries.what_makes_it_work: The hero is interactive — users can drag and manipulate the demo directly in the landing page. This makes the product's core claim (interactivity) the first thing users experience, not just read about.

entries.name: Warp Terminal
entries.what_makes_it_work: A very deliberate choice to use a single, specific gradient hue (blue-violet leaning cooler than typical) that reads as uniquely their own. Navigation items have strong typographic weighting that treats them as content, not just wayfinding.

entries.name: Rauno Freiberg Portfolio
entries.what_makes_it_work: Radical restraint — no images, no color, no decorative elements. Pure typographic system where spacing and rhythm do all the compositional work. Every design decision is a subtraction.

entries.name: Basement Studio
entries.what_makes_it_work: Uses heavy, expressive display typography at sizes that feel uncomfortable in the best way. The text itself becomes the visual element, not a header above the visual. Grunge texture applied to smooth 3D work creates productive visual tension.

entries.name: Cron Calendar
entries.what_makes_it_work: The product screenshots are at 1:1 scale and perfectly OS-contextual — they look like actual native apps, not marketing mockups. This trust signal is architectural: no chrome, no device frames.

entries.name: Ghost Publishing
entries.what_makes_it_work: Every typographic decision speaks directly to the audience (writers) — the type is beautiful because the product is about beautiful type. The spacing is generous because reading requires breathing room. The design IS the product demonstration.

entries.name: Monzo Bank
entries.what_makes_it_work: A coral/hot coral brand color (#FF3464) that is genuinely distinctive in fintech — it breaks every convention of banking safety-blue while remaining approachable. Used with discipline: coral appears only on brand elements, never as background.

entries.name: Read.cv
entries.what_makes_it_work: Uses a deliberately aged paper texture as primary background — a 'wrong' choice that reads as deeply intentional for a platform about human work histories. Typography is small and dense in a platform that could have done large and airy.

entries.name: Raycast
entries.what_makes_it_work: The gradient background is not a background — it's a haze, applied subtly so the product UI appears to float in a void. The void is the point: the tool is meant to disappear, and the design makes you feel its philosophy.

entries.name: Notion Homepage
entries.what_makes_it_work: The near-total absence of brand color is itself the brand statement — Notion is a blank canvas, and its marketing mirrors that. The visual variety comes entirely from user-created content shown in screenshots.

entries.name: Pika Labs
entries.what_makes_it_work: The homepage itself is a video product demo — the hero background cycles through AI-generated video clips. The visitor is inside the product experience before they've read a single word.

entries.name: Cosmos Design
entries.what_makes_it_work: Navigation is completely absent from the initial viewport — visitors are trusted to scroll. The entire first screen is devoted to a single, well-chosen image that communicates the platform's curatorial voice without text.

entries.name: Oxide Computer
entries.what_makes_it_work: The color palette (amber on very dark brown) is technically derived from actual terminal aesthetics — it's a period-appropriate reference that is completely authentic to the hardware being sold. Zero decoration that isn't load-bearing.

entries.name: Mailchimp
entries.what_makes_it_work: A banana yellow (#FFE01B) that no one else uses in the email marketing space. Applied lavishly as background, not just accent. The type is Helvetica-adjacent, creating a productive tension between the playful color and the serious typeface.

entries.name: Superhuman
entries.what_makes_it_work: Uses animated keyboard shortcuts as the hero visual — immediately communicating the product's core promise (speed through keyboard mastery) as an experience, not a claim. Invitation-only positioning reinforced by restrained, confident design.

entries.name: Stripe Press
entries.what_makes_it_work: Uses a publishing house's visual language (real cover photography, generous whitespace, editorial typographic scale) applied with ruthless precision. The color palette literally comes from the book covers shown, not from a brand guide.

entries.name: Tailwind UI
entries.what_makes_it_work: The product IS the component catalog — the homepage is literally a browsable library of components. The design of the page serves the product's purpose (showing components) so directly that the marketing and the product become one.

entries.name: Fey App
entries.what_makes_it_work: The hero is a live rendering of actual market data — real numbers, real charts, in real-time. This is not a screenshot or illustration; it's the product running. For a finance tool, this is the highest possible trust signal.

entries.name: Bezel App
entries.what_makes_it_work: Every screenshot is presented in a precise device frame — but the frame colors and finishes are chosen to complement the screenshot's content, not default to the standard silver iPhone. The craft is in the curated match.

entries.name: Basement Studio — Work Page
entries.what_makes_it_work: Case study titles are typeset at 15vw or larger — the type bleeds past the viewport edge on purpose, creating tension between the type wanting to escape and the frame containing it.

entries.name: Tinybird
entries.what_makes_it_work: Uses a warm off-white, but breaks expectation by applying a grid overlay that references engineering graph paper — the surface itself encodes the product's technical identity. Color comes from actual SQL query syntax highlighting, not from a brand palette.
